# Native feature-maturity documentation

`make linux-feature-maturity` and `make linux-feature-maturity-check` now invoke `mluva-feature-maturity`, a development-only Rust command. It renders the native application's existing capability registry and writes/checks the same `docs/feature-maturity.md`. The Make targets no longer initialize a Python environment. The legacy complete Linux gate calls that same native check; the obsolete Python command and its now-unused renderer are removed. Application labels and the generated document are unchanged. The development command is outside the runtime package's explicit nine-executable set.

## Independent output and command behavior

The unchanged reference is v1.6.0 at `5202477edfe4b5d8bacfa5b2e9fd6eadd9624f7f`. Its generated document SHA-256 is `5b17a6c8b417d80b3b2471b238c6864846a0b8d4a646cfcc67eb94366e1ffe12`, verified against the Git blob and actual released `--write` output. The retired script SHA-256 is `d71dad891e428dbb8ff277995cd353dec885a4eea30a96e91cddc1d9d645908f`.

The temporary reference observer executes the unchanged released script in a read-only filesystem view with a private output directory. Missing-document checking returns 1 with the existing Make advice and creates no file; writing produces the exact released bytes; checking succeeds silently; checking an edited file returns 1 and preserves the edit. Evidence is `tmp/maturity-reference-final.log` and `tmp/maturity-reference.MNLnuRXO/`. The observer stays in ignored `tmp/verify-maturity-reference.sh`; an initial invocation's unnecessary `uv --no-sync` warning was removed before the accepted run.

The native `maturity_cli` test exercises the actual executable through the same private filesystem boundary and compares the written document to the immutable Git SHA-256. It protects generated acceptance labels/order/text and non-destructive drift detection through the public CLI; it does not compare an expectation generated by Rust. The existing native Capture preferences evidence retains the UI-label contract. No production test flag, path override or extra renderer export is introduced. The standard Make check also succeeds against the unchanged checked-in document.

## Tooling and validation

The manual-only Fedora workflow now installs the compiler prerequisites and uses Fedora's [rustup package](https://packages.fedoraproject.org/pkgs/rustup/rustup/fedora-44.html), whose entry point is `rustup-init`, to prepare the repository's existing pinned Rust 1.95 toolchain. [SQLite development files](https://packages.fedoraproject.org/pkgs/sqlite/sqlite-devel/), GCC and pkg-config support the core crate's existing system-library dependency. No hosted workflow was started; this configuration change does not establish fresh Fedora acceptance.

`tmp/maturity-native-final.log` records the native command check. `tmp/maturity-linux-gate-final.log` records the actual `make linux-test` target: native generated-file check, 628 remaining legacy tests passed, Ruff passed and 170 Python files already formatted. The existing PyGObject deprecation warning remains. The first local legacy run failed because this deeply nested checkout's default temporary socket path exceeded `AF_UNIX`'s limit; the accepted run uses `PYTEST_ADDOPTS="--basetemp=$PWD/tmp/py"`. No product behavior or test assertion was changed for that harness limit.

The complete native workspace passes 139 tests, zero failures and 61 ignored environment checks across 97 suites (`tmp/maturity-workspace.log`), with strict all-target Clippy (`tmp/maturity-clippy.log`). Both actual Make generation/check targets preserve the checked-in document (`tmp/maturity-make.log`); the required private-bus shortcut gate also passes (`tmp/maturity-shortcut-gate.log`). Formatting, diff and the documented ShellCheck gate pass. The broad shell check found an unused loop variable in the existing private browser runner; naming it as intentionally unused preserves the loop and resolves that warning.

The generated labels are still the immutable released application's acceptance registry; this conversion does not promote native parity. Remaining development/runtime Python and the full application/distribution acceptance gates are tracked in the parity matrix.
